name: Study buddy
oneLine: Your notes become a quiz you can play.
forWho: Students and anyone with a test coming up who has notes but no time to make flashcards.
youGet: A quiz that asks why, not just what
Flashcards from your key words
Missed questions come back until they stick
woah: It brings back the ones you got wrong, like a tutor.
whyBetter: Plain Claude asks easy recall questions, adds facts your notes never said, and forgets your misses. This sticks to your notes and drills misses.
tryPrompt: Turn my notes into a quiz I can practice with. Here are my notes:
request:
can you make me a quiz from my notes? science test on friday

Water cycle notes, Year 8 science

- Water moves between the sea, the air and the land in a loop called the water cycle. The sun powers it.
- Evaporation: the sun heats water in seas, lakes and rivers and it turns into water vapour (a gas) that rises.
- Transpiration: plants lose water vapour through tiny holes in their leaves. Evaporation + transpiration together = evapotranspiration.
- Condensation: as water vapour rises the air gets colder, so the vapour cools and turns back into tiny liquid droplets. Lots of droplets make clouds.
- Precipitation: when droplets join and get too heavy they fall as rain, snow, sleet or hail.
- Collection: water that falls collects in oceans, lakes and rivers. Some runs over the ground (surface runoff) into rivers.
- Infiltration: some water soaks into the ground and becomes groundwater. It can stay there a long time and slowly flows back to rivers and the sea.
- About 97% of Earth's water is salty sea water. Only about 3% is fresh water and most of that is frozen in ice caps and glaciers.
- Warmer temperatures mean more evaporation.
- Trees cut down = less transpiration, so the air above can get drier. (check this w/ Mr Patel)
- The total amount of water on Earth stays about the same, it just changes state and place.
- Key words: state change, water vapour, runoff, groundwater, reservoir (a store of water like a lake or an ice cap)

result.reason: the skill gives instant per-question feedback quoting the student's own notes, retries misses, and skips the unverified Mr Patel note; plain Claude is accurate and includes short-answer questions and a helpful Mr Patel flag, but it is static, so the student has to mark themselves.

A month calendar and gentle stats
Streaks that survive one missed day

tryPrompt: Make me a habit tracker. My habits are:

result.reason: the skill is forgiving (return ticket, backfill past days), lets users add, edit and delete habits, offers export and import, and is built for a phone; plain Claude has hardcoded habits, no streak forgiveness, a month grid that cuts off on a phone screen, and its water cups conflict with the habit check-off.
